title: Geometric connectedness can be checked after a field extension
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-pc-field-extension], let $X$ be a scheme over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base], and let $k'/k$ be a field extension. Regard the base change $X_{k'}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k'$ [def-pc-base-change] as a scheme over $k'$ through its projection to $\operatorname{Spec}k'$. Then $X$ is geometrically connected over $k$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] if and only if $X_{k'}$ is geometrically connected over $k'$.

mathlib_searches.query: geometric connectedness can be checked after a field extension

proof.text: Assume $X$ is geometrically connected over $k$. For every field extension $L/k$, the base change $X_L$ is connected by the definition of geometric connectedness. For a field extension $k'/k$, the base change $(X_{k'})_L$ is canonically $X_L$ over $L$, so the same condition holds for $X_{k'}$ over $k'$.

source.place: Lemma 33.7.3, tag 054N, proof of the forward implication

proof.text: Conversely, assume $X_{k'}$ is geometrically connected over $k'$, and let $k''/k$ be arbitrary. By [lem-weil-common-extension-fields] there is a field $k'''$ with embeddings of $k'$ and $k''$ over $k$. The iterated base-change identification gives $X_{k'''}=(X_{k'})_{k'''}$, which is connected because $X_{k'}$ is geometrically connected and $k'''/k'$ is a field extension.

source.place: Lemma 33.7.3, tag 054N, proof of the converse (common extension)

proof.text: The morphism $\operatorname{Spec}(k''')\to\operatorname{Spec}(k'')$ is surjective, both spaces being one point. By the base-change identification $X_{k'''}=X_{k''}\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k''}\operatorname{Spec}k'''$, the projection $X_{k'''}\to X_{k''}$ is the base change of this surjective morphism, hence is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. The continuous image of the connected space $X_{k'''}$ is therefore the connected space $X_{k''}$. Since $k''/k$ was arbitrary, $X$ is geometrically connected over $k$.
